hero.h1: Plumbing Maintenance and Inspections in Arlington Heights, IL
hero.sub: Most plumbing emergencies give a warning first: a sump pump that's getting loud, a water heater that's making noise or a slow drain that keeps coming back. A maintenance visit catches those early. From our office on East Central Road.

blocks.intro: We look at the whole system:

steps.body: Age, leaks, relief valve, venting and sediment, with a flush if it's due.
A test cycle, the float, the check valve and the battery backup if you have one.
Slow drains, gurgling and a [camera inspection](/arlington-heights/video-camera-sewer-inspections) if something looks off.
Galvanized or copper condition, leaks and shutoff valves that may not close.
Running toilets, dripping faucets and worn supply lines.
What's fine, what to plan for and what needs attention now.

blocks.h2: Why Maintenance Matters in Arlington Heights Homes
blocks.intro: About 3 in 4 homes here were built between 1940 and 1989. Most have reached the age where small issues are worth catching early.

items.h3: Postwar Plumbing at the End of Its Life
items.body: Homes from the 1940s through the 1960s often have clay sewer lines, cast iron drains and galvanized supply pipe. A checkup tells you which parts are wearing out before one fails.

items.h3: 1970s and 1980s Homes, Second Round of Equipment
items.body: Homes from these decades are on their second or third water heater and sump pump. Knowing their age helps you replace them on your schedule.
A spring visit tests the sump pump, the backup and the floor drain before heavy rain arrives. The July 2011 storm showed how fast a basement can flood.
Main and fixture shutoffs in older homes often haven't been turned in years. We test them so they work when you need them.

blocks.h2: Plumbing Maintenance Questions From Arlington Heights Homeowners

items.q: How often should I have my plumbing inspected?
items.preview: Once a year is a good rule, ideally in spring.
items.answer: Once a year is a good rule for most Arlington Heights homes. Spring works well because it lets us test the sump pump before storm season.

items.q: Is an inspection worth it if nothing is wrong?
items.preview: Yes. The point is to find problems before they become emergencies.
items.answer: Yes. Most plumbing failures give small warning signs first. An inspection catches them while they're cheap to fix and on your schedule.

items.q: What does a maintenance visit include?
items.preview: Water heater, pumps, drains, pipes, valves and fixtures, plus a written summary.
items.answer: We check the water heater, sump and ejector pumps, drains, supply pipes, shutoff valves and fixtures, and give you a summary of what we found.

items.preview: Yes. The No Drip Club is our yearly maintenance plan.
items.answer: Yes. The [No Drip Club](/no-drip-club) is our yearly plan that brings a plumber to your home for regular maintenance.

items.q: How much does a plumbing inspection cost in Arlington Heights?
items.preview: It depends on the home and what's included. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the size of the home and what's included, like a sewer camera inspection or a water heater flush. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
